references.text: Earlier in the same chapter it is explained how touching dead animals makes one unclean until evening, and that one must wash their clothes.
The continuation of the same paragraph elaborating on how uncleanness spreads to objects that come into contact with the dead creeping things.
A parallel law regarding uncleanness until evening for anyone who enters a house declared unclean.
Similar provisions concerning uncleanness until evening upon touching, requiring washing of oneself and one's clothes.
A law stating that eating animals that died naturally or were torn apart makes one unclean until evening.
Priests become unclean until evening through contact with creeping things and must cleanse themselves before they may eat the holy offerings.
An expanded law concerning uncleanness from touching dead people, lasting seven days and requiring purification.
Reiteration of the prohibition against eating unclean animals and touching their dead bodies.
The prophet Haggai asks the priests about the transmission of uncleanness through contact, based on the principles in Leviticus.
